questions.stem: Which of the following are branches of anterior division of the internal iliac artery?Superior gluteal arteryInferior gluteal arterySuperior vesical arteryMiddle rectal arteryInferior vesical arteryVaginal arterySelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
2,3,4,5,6

The nine branches of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery may be more easily remembered in these divisions:

  • "three urinary": umbilical artery, superior vesical artery, inferior vesical artery
  • "three visceral": uterine artery, vaginal artery, middle rectal artery
  • "three parietal": obturator artery, internal pudendal artery, inferior gluteal artery

Branches of Posterior division

  • Iliolumbar artery
  • Lateral sacral arteries

Superior gluteal artery




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice - 42nd edition - page 1309.

questions.stem: In a subclavian artery block at the outer border of 1st rib, which of the following arteries help in maintaining the circulation to the upper limb?Suprascapular arterySuperior thoracic arteryThyrocervical trunkSubscapular arterySelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1,3 and 4
  • A rich anastomosis exists around the scapula between branches of the subclavian artery (first part) and the axillary artery (third part).
  • This anastomosis provides a collateral circulation through which blood can flow to the limb when the distal part of subclavian artery or the proximal part of axillary artery is blocked.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No.80,81.

questions.stem: A male patient who has already taken the first dose for COVID vaccine comes for the second dose. The health worker then noticed that his shoulder was flat, flabby and looked asymmetrical due to loss of contour. Which of these structures would have been injured to lead to this scenario?
questions.solutionHtml:
Deltoid
  • Given scenario is typical for shoulder dislocation.
  • On examination, there is often an asymmetrywith the contralateral side. Often there is a loss of shoulder contours (from a ‘flattened deltoid’) and an anterior bulge from the head of the humerus may also be seen.
  • It is important to assess the neurovascular status of the arm, which can become compromised in some cases, especially the axillary and suprascapular nerves.


Gray's Anatomy for Students International Edition, 4th Edition Page No.714.

questions.stemHtml: A neonate develops RDS. Which of the following areas have problems?
questions.solutionHtml:
C

Given image shows an electron microscopic view of alveolus and its structures.

  • Respiratory distress syndrome is caused due to abnormality of type II pneumocytes.
  • Given image shows an electron microscopic view of alveolus and its structures.
  • The interstitium at is tissue between two layers of alveolar epithelial cells containing elastic and collagen fibers produced by fibroblasts (also known as septal cells). There is no connective tissue over the capillaries. 



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice - 42nd edition, Page No- 373.

questions.stemHtml: A patient with a fall from a height was treated with a cast. After removal of the cast, he was not able to walk properly, unable to lift his leg and was dragging his right leg while walking. Which of the following marked structures is involved?
questions.solutionHtml:
A
  • Here, the case scenario points to a possible injury to gluteus medius which is causing lurching gait and dragging of feet in the patient.
  • Dissected right gluteal region has been shown in the image.

PM: piriformis muscle; SN: sciatic nerve; GM: gluteus medius; SGN: superior gluteal nerve; *: additional belly of piriformis muscle

  • Abductors of hip are – Gluteus medius and minimus (main)
  • Tensor fascia lata and sartorius (accessory)

The left gluteal region after reflecting gluteus maximus muscle

Figure: The left gluteal region after reflecting gluteus maximus muscle; CFn — common fibular nerve; Tn — tibial nerve; IGv — inferior gluteal vessels; Pfm — piriformis muscle; GM — gluteus medius; QF — quadratus femoris muscle; GMx — gluteus maximus muscle; Sn — sciatic nerve.

questions.stemHtml: The following cell marked as A is inhibitory to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Deep nuclei of cerebellum

Cell marked as A is Purkinje cell in cerebellar cortex and it is inhibitory to deep cerebellar nuclei.

Axons of Purkinje cells are inhibitory. They project to and inhibit the deep cerebellar nuclei.

questions.stem: Inferior thyroid artery supplies which of these parts-Thyroid glandParathyroid glandOesophagusThymusSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1,2,3,4
  • The inferior thyroid artery is the principal blood supplier of the thyroid gland (supplies the lower half).
  • The ITA gives rise to the ascending cervical artery, the inferior laryngeal artery, and also gives pharyngeal, tracheal, and esophageal branches.
  • Also, the ITA supplies the four parathyroid glands.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice - 42nd edition page No-1464.e86.

questions.stemHtml: 3rd part of the vertebral artery is related to which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
B
  • Given image shows the 1st cervical vertebra also known as atlas.
  • 3rd part of the vertebral artery is related to the posterior arch of atlas.
  • V3 (extradural or extraspinal) curves and twists across the top of the C1 vertebra (the atlas) until it enters the skull. V4 (intradural or intracranial) enters the skull. The right and left vertebral arteries then join together to form the basilar artery.

questions.stemHtml: Which part of the scapula is seen in infraclavicular fossa?
questions.solutionHtml:
A
  • The coracoid process is an osseous structure that arises from the superior border of the head of the scapula, projecting forward and curving laterally.
  • The coracoid process is located directly below the lateral fourth of the clavicleand connected to its under surface by the coracoclavicular ligament.
  • Coracoid process is seen and palpated in infraclavicular fossa.
  • This can be seen retrospectively as :The boundaries of the infraclavicular fossaare the pectoralis minor and major muscles anteriorly, ribs medially, clavicle and CORACOID PROCESS SUPERIORLY.

SCAPULA
